name: Eliehoenai
overview: Eliehoenai was a male Levite known as the seventh-born son of Meshelemiah, also called Shallum, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 26:3. His identification within the tribe of Levi situates him among the priestly lineage, though no additional personal notes are provided in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliehoenai means 'my eyes [look] to YHWH,' reflecting a devotional focus on the Lord. This proper name, given by his parents rather than directly by God, highlights a spiritual aspiration consistent with his Levitical heritage.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Eliehoenai as the son of Shallum (Meshelemiah). Beyond this paternal connection, no other familial relationships are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Eliehoenai's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the Levitical priestly families, specifically as a descendant of Meshelemiah. This lineage underscores the continuity of those set apart for temple service and worship in Israel, emphasizing faithfulness to God's covenant through the tribe of Levi.
